messages:
jamie.dev: Quick sync — I'm prototyping the 'policy editor' for tier+region routing + model-variant fallback. Need input on quota semantics and telemetry we should surface in Console.

sasha: Do we want quotas to be token-based or request-based by default? free customers are bursty, pro/enterprise care about token spend.

mike_infra: token-based makes billing simpler, but enforcement at token granularity is heavier on the router. Could we do hybrid: soft token limit then request-level hard cap?

lee_pm: From UX POV we need to make "soft vs hard" obvious. Soft = degrade (fallback), hard = block (429). We should show inline examples in the editor.

jessie_ml: For fallback behavior we need to think about model-variant compatibility. e.g. fallback from gptx-16k -> gptx-8k-quantized is ok for many apps but might break structured outputs. Need a way to tag variants with "lossy:true" so users can opt-in.

jamie.dev: Agree. Proposal sketch: policy object has per-tier entries, region overrides, quota policy, and fallback chain with reasons. Example blob below (for discussion):

```json
{
  "policy_id": "policy-2026-03-routing",
  "tiers": {
    "free": {
      "quota": {"type": "soft", "unit": "tokens", "limit": 100000},
      "route": [{"model": "small-1q", "weight": 100}],
      "fallbacks": ["small-1q", "small-1-int8"]
    },
    "pro": {
      "quota": {"type": "soft", "unit": "tokens", "limit": 2000000},
      "route": [{"model": "gptx-8k", "weight": 80}, {"model": "gptx-8k-quant", "weight": 20}],
      "fallbacks": ["gptx-8k", "gptx-8k-quant"]
    },
    "enterprise": {
      "quota": {"type": "hard", "unit": "requests", "limit": 0},
      "route": [{"model": "gptx-16k", "weight": 100}],
      "fallbacks": []
    }
  },
  "regions": {
    "eu": {"overrides": {"pro": {"route": [{"model": "gptx-eu-8k", "weight": 100}]}}}
  }
}
```

jamie.dev: Note: enterprise quota.limit=0 means unlimited (we use 0 as sentinel).

taylor_ops: Nice. A few operational questions: how does enforcement happen on rollout? If we change fallback chains, do we backfill telemetry? We need a stable version id for policies so we can map past telemetry to the exact config.

mike_infra: store policy artifacts in config-service with content-hash id. Router adds policy_id + policy_hash to trace spans. Telemetry table keys: policy_hash, model_variant, tenant_id, region, outcome. That lets Console show "fallback_rate for config vX".

lee_pm: UX for rollouts — we should let users do percent rollouts by tenant cohorts and have an automatic rollback if quality evals regress. Console widget: slider for percent, preview of affected tenants, and button for "auto rollback on eval\".

jessie_ml: Regarding quality evals: we can surface evals from Redwood Optimize linked to a rollout. If fallback ratio spikes > X% or eval NLL degrades beyond threshold then mark for rollback. Need a reliable signal (not just latency).

sasha: Back to quotas: If soft quota is reached, router should prefer fallbacks and continue serving. But we should also surface a top-level webhook/event for billing pipeline so customers can be notified when they're near limits.

jamie.dev: Agreed. Implement event types: quota.warning, quota.soft-exhausted, quota.hard-exhausted. They include policy_hash, tier, tenant_id, remaining_units.

mike_infra: Also propose we expose metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency per route, fallback_count, fallback_ratio (fallback_count / total_requests), cost_per_1000_tokens, and request_denied_count. Keep these in Console under per-policy -> per-tenant views.

lee_pm: For the editor UI, do we want both a form-based and raw JSON view? Form for common patterns, JSON for advanced. And a "simulate" button where you paste a sample request (tenant+region+tokens+expected_output-type) and get the routing decision and why.

taylor_ops: Simulation + dry-run rollout would help SREs. Also want audit logs of policy changes and ability to pin a policy version for a tenant.

jessie_ml: One caution: fallback chains should be explicit and include compatibility tags. Example: {"model":"gptx-8k-quant","compatibility":["text","summaries"],"lossy":true}. Router rejects fallback if tenant requested a strict "structured" output contract unless tenant opts in.

jamie.dev: Good call. I'll add compatibility tags. Also need to decide default behavior for mixed-weight routes. If route weights sum to 100, fallback should respect weights only among available models; if none available follow fallback chain.

sasha: Is there a single API endpoint to update a policy? PATCH vs PUT? PATCH for small edits, PUT for full replace. Need to document merge semantics for tier and region overrides.

mike_infra: Suggest POST /policies (create), PUT /policies/:id (replace), PATCH /policies/:id (merge). Also GET /policies/:id?version=hash for historical. Router caches policy id+hash and invalidates on change.

jamie.dev: Action items I hear: 1) I will update schema to include compatibility tags + soft/hard sentinel docs. 2) mike_infra will design telemetry keys to include policy_hash. 3) lee_pm to mock editor UX (form + JSON + simulate). 4) taylor_ops to specify audit events and webhooks for quota. 5) jessie_ml to produce guidance for safe fallback chains and compatibility mappings.

deploy-bot: deploy accepted: policy-editor-service v0.9.1 -> staging at 2026-03-12T15:22:10Z :rocket:

jamie.dev: Thanks — tagging @sasha @mike_infra @lee_pm for follow-ups. I'll push an updated draft to the RFC repo tomorrow and add sample console mockups.

sasha: SGTM. One more: let's make sure tenant-level overrides can be set but we require enterprise approval for >30% weight changes to protect SREs from noisy tenants.

jamie.dev: Noted. We'll add an approval workflow for tenant-weight mutations.

mike_infra: I'll start a telemetry sketch in the infra repo and ping for review.

lee_pm: I'll prototype the simulate flow in Figma and include example requests.

jessie_ml: I'll write a short doc on "fallback safety" patterns for devs.

jamie.dev: Cool — closing this thread for now, will post RFC link when ready.
